findings.title: Server-Side JavaScript Injection via eval() in contribution percentages
findings.attack_path: Authenticated user submits POST /contributions with preTax/afterTax/roth set to a JavaScript payload (e.g. 'require("child_process").execSync("id")'). handleContributionsUpdate runs eval(req.body.preTax) on the raw string with no sanitization, executing arbitrary code in the Node process. NaN checks run after eval, so payloads with side effects already executed.

findings.title: NoSQL injection via unsanitized $where clause in allocations threshold
findings.attack_path: Attacker calls GET /allocations/:userId?threshold=0';while(true){} . AllocationsDAO.getByUserIdAndThreshold interpolates the raw threshold into a Mongo $where string `this.userId == X && this.stocks > '${threshold}'`, which MongoDB evaluates as JavaScript. Payloads enable boolean-blind data extraction across all users or a server-side infinite-loop DoS.

findings.title: User passwords stored and compared in cleartext
findings.attack_path: UserDAO.addUser inserts password as the plaintext request value; validateLogin compares with `fromDB === fromUser`. Any read of the users collection (NoSQL injection, backup leak, compromised DB host, malicious insider) immediately yields every user's usable password, enabling account takeover and credential reuse against other systems.

findings.title: Sensitive PII (SSN, DOB, bank account, routing) stored unencrypted
findings.attack_path: ProfileDAO.updateUser writes ssn, dob, bankAcc, bankRouting directly to the users document; the encryption helpers are commented out. Combined with NoSQL injection or any database exposure, an attacker exfiltrates regulated financial PII in cleartext.

findings.title: Default hardcoded admin and user credentials seeded into the database
findings.attack_path: artifacts/db-reset.js seeds admin/Admin_123, user1/User1_123, user2/User2_123 in cleartext. An unauthenticated attacker logs in at POST /login with the well-known default admin password, gaining full administrative access including the benefits management functions.

findings.title: Server-Side Request Forgery in /research stock lookup
findings.attack_path: Authenticated user requests GET /research?symbol=x&url=http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/ . ResearchHandler concatenates req.query.url + req.query.symbol and fetches it server-side with needle, writing the raw body back to the response. Attacker reaches cloud metadata, internal admin services, and localhost-only endpoints, and reads the responses.

findings.title: Stored and reflected XSS due to globally disabled template auto-escaping
findings.attack_path: swig.setDefaults({autoescape:false}) disables HTML escaping for all {{ }} output. An attacker stores a script payload in profile firstName/lastName (rendered in layout nav and allocations view) or the address field; when a victim or admin views the page the script executes in their session, enabling session-cookie theft (cookie lacks httpOnly) and admin compromise.

findings.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference exposes any user's allocations
findings.attack_path: GET /allocations/:userId takes userId from the URL path, not the session. AllocationsHandler.displayAllocations passes it straight to the DAO with no ownership check, so an authenticated attacker enumerates /allocations/1, /allocations/2, ... to read every user's financial allocation and identity fields.

findings.title: Missing function-level access control on benefits administration
findings.attack_path: GET/POST /benefits are protected only by isLoggedIn; the isAdmin middleware exists but is not wired in (the admin-gated route is commented out). Any authenticated non-admin user lists all employees and rewrites benefitStartDate values via POST /benefits, an admin-only function.

findings.title: No CSRF protection on state-changing POST endpoints
findings.attack_path: csurf is imported but the middleware and token generation are commented out; templates emit an empty {{csrftoken}}. An attacker lures a logged-in victim to a malicious page that auto-submits a form to POST /profile, /contributions, /benefits, or /memos, performing actions (including the eval() and benefit-tampering paths) as the victim.

findings.title: Session fixation and insecure session cookie configuration
findings.attack_path: handleLoginRequest sets req.session.userId without calling req.session.regenerate(), so a pre-set session id survives authentication (session fixation). The session cookie has no httpOnly, secure, or maxAge flags and the app runs over plaintext HTTP, so a fixed or sniffed cookie yields full account access.

findings.title: Open redirect in /learn endpoint
findings.attack_path: GET /learn?url=https://evil.example redirects with res.redirect(req.query.url) and no allowlist. Attacker crafts a trusted-looking nodegoat link that bounces victims to a phishing or malware site, lending the redirect the application's credibility.

findings.title: Regular Expression Denial of Service in bank routing validation
findings.attack_path: handleProfileUpdate validates bankRouting with /([0-9]+)+\#/, which has catastrophic backtracking. A POST /profile with bankRouting set to a long digit string without the trailing '#' (e.g. many 9s) makes the regex consume CPU exponentially, blocking the single-threaded Node event loop and degrading service for all users.

findings.title: Hardcoded session and crypto secrets committed in configuration
findings.attack_path: config/config.js hardcodes cookieSecret 'session_cookie_secret_key_here' and cryptoKey 'a_secure_key_for_crypto_here' in source control. With the session-signing secret known, an attacker forges valid signed session cookies for arbitrary users (including admin) and, if the commented crypto were enabled, the static key plus reused IV would render PII encryption ineffective.

findings.title: Application served over plaintext HTTP with no security headers
findings.attack_path: server.js starts http.createServer (HTTPS block commented out) and all helmet middleware (HSTS, CSP, frameguard, noCache, nosniff) is disabled. Credentials, session cookies, SSN and bank data traverse the network in cleartext; a network MITM captures sessions and PII, and the missing CSP/frameguard amplify the XSS and clickjacking surface. Unused TLS keys sit in artifacts/cert.

findings.title: Weak password policy and username enumeration at authentication
findings.attack_path: validateSignup permits 1-20 char passwords with no complexity rule, and handleLoginRequest returns distinct 'Invalid username' vs 'Invalid password' messages. There is no rate limiting or lockout. An attacker enumerates valid usernames, then brute-forces weak passwords (or default seeded ones) unimpeded.

findings.title: Outdated and vulnerable dependencies including EOL Node runtime
findings.attack_path: package.json pins marked 0.3.5, mongodb 2.x, swig 1.4.2 and other long-unmaintained packages; Dockerfile builds on end-of-life node:12-alpine. Published CVEs in these versions (e.g. marked ReDoS/XSS bypasses) are exploitable through user-controlled input rendered by the app.

findings.title: Verbose error responses disclose stack traces
findings.attack_path: The error middleware renders the full error object to error-template and logs err.stack. Triggering an unhandled error (malformed input to any route) returns internal paths, dependency versions, and query structure that aid an attacker in tailoring NoSQL/SSJS injection payloads.

findings.title: Markdown rendering of shared memos enables HTML/content injection
findings.attack_path: POST /memos stores arbitrary memo text into a shared, unattributed memos collection; memos.html renders it with marked(doc.memo). marked is configured with sanitize:true (partial mitigation), but the deprecated 0.3.5 sanitizer has known bypasses and the shared board lets any user inject markdown/HTML viewed by every other user, supporting phishing links and stored-content tampering.

findings.title: Log injection / CRLF forging via unsanitized username in auth logs
findings.attack_path: On a failed login handleLoginRequest logs the raw userName ('attempt to login with invalid user: ' + userName) with no CRLF stripping. An attacker submits a username containing newlines and forged log lines to inject fabricated entries, hampering incident response and breaking log-integrity assumptions.

findings.title: NoSQL operator injection at login via object-typed username
findings.attack_path: validateLogin passes req.body.userName straight into usersCol.findOne({userName: userName}). bodyParser/JSON allows an attacker to send userName as an object such as {"$gt":""} (or {"$ne":null}); the operator matches a user document and, paired with a similarly crafted password match or the cleartext comparison, can bypass intended authentication semantics and select arbitrary accounts.
